query: For MnNiSi-based magnetic-refrigeration materials, what single intervention could improve mechanical performance while retaining a large magnetocaloric effect? cited_evidence.text: AbstractThe composition of grain boundaries (GBs) determines their mechanical behavior, which in turn affects the mechanical properties of nanocrystalline materials. Inspired by GB segregation and the concept of high-entropy alloys (HEAs), we investigated, respectively, the mechanical responses of nanocrystalline Cu samples with and without multi-element GBs, as well as the grain size effects, aiming to explore the effects of GB composition decoration on mechanical properties. Our results show that introducing multi-element segregation GBs can significantly improve the mechanical properties of nanocrystalline Cu by effectively inhibiting GB migration and sliding. Additionally, we proposed an improved a theoretical model that can reasonably describe the strengths of the materials with multi-element or single-element segregation GBs. Notably, the introduction of multi-element segregation GBs inhibits both migration and sliding behavior, with migration being more effectively suppressed than sliding. decision.trend: Research has been focused on improving the mechanical performance of high-entropy alloys (HEAs) while retaining their unique properties, such as magnetocaloric effect. Various approaches have been explored, including composition changes, processing routes, and thermomechanical treatments. The trend suggests that introducing defects, such as ordered dislocations, and optimizing the microstructure through thermomechanical processing can lead to improved mechanical properties.
decision.unsolved: The challenge of improving mechanical performance while retaining a large magnetocaloric effect in MnNiSi-based magnetic-refrigeration materials remains unsolved. The current research has not yet found a single intervention that can achieve this goal without compromising either property.
decision.why: Introducing ordered dislocations has been shown to improve mechanical properties in other high-entropy alloys, and this approach may be applicable to MnNiSi-based materials. Additionally, optimizing the microstructure through thermomechanical processing has been successful in improving mechanical properties in other HEAs, making it a plausible next step for MnNiSi-based materials.
